title: NovaDirective
description: What Nova is permitted to say and do, decided by the Decision Engine rather than by a prompt. A prompt is a preference; this is a guarantee — `mayNameMisconception` is false unless a misconception cleared the actionable threshold, so 'you don't understand X' is unreachable without evidence rather than merely discouraged.

mode.description: ask = we do not know why they are failing, so questions only. explain = an actionable misconception exists, teach that one thing. withhold = they are close, a bigger hint takes it off them. direct = they have done this unaided, be brief.

mayNameMisconception.description: True only under REMEDIATE, which requires an actionable misconception to exist.

namedMisconception.description: A failure class the verification engine emitted, never a label this system invented. Null whenever mayNameMisconception is false.

maxHintLevel.description: Ceiling on the hint ladder. 0 = questions only. DIAGNOSE sets 0 because a hint given without a diagnosis is a guess in a confident voice.

mustNotSay.description: Always contains the shaming sentences and their variants. Carried into every grant, including a learner override — the override buys a bigger hint, not a diagnosis.

opening.description: Filled from counts. Never a claim the evidence cannot carry.

$comment: TRANSPORT SUBSET: only { max_hint_level, mode, may_include_code } crosses the network to the LLM server. The claim-bearing fields (namedMisconception, mayNameMisconception, opening) stay client-side and are RENDERED from server-computed state, never handed to a model as fact. See packages/nova-core/python/nova_directive.py.
